claim: Chemokine receptors are GPCRs that regulate the chemotactic migration of a wide variety of cells including immune and cancer cells.
source: Chemokine receptors are GPCRs that regulate the chemotactic migration of a wide variety of cells including immune and cancer cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about chemokine receptors and their function.

claim: Most chemokine receptors contain features associated with the ability to stimulate G protein signaling during β-arrestin-mediated receptor internalization into endosomes.
source: Most chemokine receptors contain features associated with the ability to stimulate G protein signaling during β-arrestin-mediated receptor internalization into endosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the analysis of chemokine receptor C-terminal tail sequences shown in Table 1, which demonstrates the presence of serine/threonine phosphorylation site clusters.

claim: Endosomal signaling of certain non-GPCR receptors plays a major role in cell migration.
source: As endosomal signaling of certain non-GPCR receptors plays a major role in cell migration, we chose to investigate the potential role of endosomal chemokine receptor signaling on mechanisms governing this function.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work on receptor tyrosine kinases mentioned in the introduction (Palamidessi et al., 2008; Schiefermeier et al., 2011).

claim: CCR7 recruits G protein and β-arrestin simultaneously upon chemokine stimulation.
source: Applying a combination of pharmacological and cell biological approaches, we demonstrate that the model chemokine receptor CCR7 recruits G protein and β-arrestin simultaneously upon chemokine stimulation
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2, including NanoBiT assays and confocal microscopy showing co-recruitment of miniGi and βarr1.

claim: Internalized CCR7 receptors activate G protein from endosomes.
source: Applying a combination of pharmacological and cell biological approaches, we demonstrate that the model chemokine receptor CCR7 recruits G protein and β-arrestin simultaneously upon chemokine stimulation, which enables internalized receptors to activate G protein from endosomes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 3 showing endosomal Gi/o activation using Rap1GAP-SmBiT/LgBiT-FYVE biosensors and miniGi translocation to endosomes.

claim: Endosomal CCR7 uniquely enriches specific Rho GTPase regulators as compared to plasma membrane CCR7.
source: Furthermore, spatiotemporal-resolved APEX2 proteome profiling shows that endosomal CCR7 uniquely enriches specific Rho GTPase regulators as compared to plasma membrane CCR7
evidence: This is supported by APEX2 proteomics data shown in Figure 5, which identifies differential enrichment of RhoGAPs, RhoGEFs, and RhoGDIs upon CCL19 vs CCL21 stimulation.

claim: Endosomal CCR7 signaling is directly associated with enhanced activity of the Rho GTPase Rac1.
source: Furthermore, spatiotemporal-resolved APEX2 proteome profiling shows that endosomal CCR7 uniquely enriches specific Rho GTPase regulators as compared to plasma membrane CCR7, which is directly associated with enhanced activity of the Rho GTPase Rac1 and chemotaxis of immune T cells.
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT assays in Figure 6 showing differential Rac1 activation by CCL19 vs CCL21, and by experiments showing that endocytosis inhibitors reduce Rac1 activation.

claim: Endosomal CCR7 signaling is associated with chemotaxis of immune T cells.
source: Furthermore, spatiotemporal-resolved APEX2 proteome profiling shows that endosomal CCR7 uniquely enriches specific Rho GTPase regulators as compared to plasma membrane CCR7, which is directly associated with enhanced activity of the Rho GTPase Rac1 and chemotaxis of immune T cells.
evidence: This is supported by transwell migration assays in Figure 7 showing that CCL19 promotes greater chemotaxis than CCL21, and that endocytosis inhibitors reduce chemotaxis.

claim: Rac1 drives the formation of membrane protrusions during chemotaxis.
source: As Rac1 drives the formation of membrane protrusions during chemotaxis, our findings suggest an important integrated function of endosomal chemokine receptor signaling in cell migration.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about Rac1 function in cell migration.

claim: There exist 23 chemokine receptors that belong to the highly druggable superfamily of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs).
source: There exist 23 chemokine receptors that belong to the highly druggable superfamily of G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the chemokine receptor family.

claim: GPCRs activate heterotrimeric G proteins (Gαβγ) at the cell surface, causing downstream signaling throughout the cell.
source: Canonically, GPCRs activate heterotrimeric G proteins (Gαβγ) at the cell surface, causing downstream signaling throughout the cell (Gilman, 1987).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gilman, 1987, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: G protein signaling is terminated via a specialized desensitization mechanism that includes phosphorylation of receptors by GPCR kinases and subsequent recruitment of β-arrestins.
source: This initial phase of G protein signaling is terminated via a specialized desensitization mechanism that includes phosphorylation of receptors by GPCR kinases and subsequent recruitment of β-arrestins (βarrs) to the phosphorylated receptor (Moore et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Moore et al., 2007, representing established knowledge.

claim: βarr recruitment to the receptor sterically blocks further G protein activation.
source: βarrs engage receptors at an overlapping transmembrane core region to where G proteins bind, and thus βarr recruitment to the receptor sterically blocks further G protein activation (Lohse et al., 1990; Lee et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Lohse et al., 1990 and Lee et al., 2020.

claim: βarrs promote the internalization of GPCRs into endosomes, thereby removing them from the source of the activating ligand.
source: In addition, βarrs promote the internalization of GPCRs into endosomes, thereby removing them from the source of the activating ligand (Goodman et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Goodman et al., 1996.

claim: Some GPCRs continue to activate G proteins following βarr-mediated internalization into endosomes.
source: In more recent times work has shown that some GPCRs continue to activate G proteins following βarr-mediated internalization into endosomes (Jensen et al., 2017; Thomsen et al., 2018; Thomsen et al., 2016; Irannejad et al., 2013; Calebiro et al., 2009; Wehbi et al., 2013; Ferrandon et al., 2009; Mullershausen et al., 2009; Flores-Espinoza and Thomsen, 2024).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work demonstrating endosomal G protein signaling.

claim: Certain GPCRs containing serine/threonine phosphorylation site clusters in their carboxy-terminal tail bind to βarrs in a 'tail conformation'.
source: However, our recent work showed that certain GPCRs containing serine/threonine phosphorylation site clusters in their carboxy-terminal tail bind to βarrs in a specific conformation termed 'tail conformation' (Cahill et al., 2017; Kumari et al., 2016; Kumari et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cahill et al., 2017; Kumari et al., 2016; Kumari et al., 2017.

claim: In the tail conformation, βarr only interacts with the receptor carboxy-terminal tail thereby permitting the receptor transmembrane core to bind to G proteins simultaneously to form a GPCR–G protein–βarr complex or 'megaplex'.
source: In this conformation, βarr only interacts with the receptor carboxy-terminal tail thereby permitting the receptor transmembrane core to bind to G proteins simultaneously to form a GPCR–G protein–βarr complex or 'megaplex' (Thomsen et al., 2016; Cahill et al., 2017; Nguyen et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Thomsen et al., 2016; Cahill et al., 2017; Nguyen et al., 2019.

claim: Most chemokine receptors couple to similar G protein subtypes.
source: Most chemokine receptors couple to similar G protein subtypes (Hughes and Nibbs, 2018) and contain serine/threonine clusters in their carboxy-terminal tail (Table 1)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hughes and Nibbs, 2018.

claim: Most chemokine receptors contain serine/threonine clusters in their carboxy-terminal tail.
source: Most chemokine receptors couple to similar G protein subtypes (Hughes and Nibbs, 2018) and contain serine/threonine clusters in their carboxy-terminal tail (Table 1)
evidence: This is supported by the data presented in Table 1, which shows the C-terminal sequences of chemokine receptors with serine/threonine clusters highlighted.

claim: CCR7 is expressed by several subsets of immune cells and regulates their homing to the lymph nodes.
source: To study the potential role of endosomal chemokine receptor signaling we used the model receptor CCR7, which is expressed by several subsets of immune cells and regulates their homing to the lymph nodes (Förster et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Förster et al., 2008.

claim: CCR7 is known to be active at endomembranes.
source: This receptor is an ideal model receptor to study endosomal G protein signaling as it is known to be active at endomembranes (Laufer et al., 2019)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Laufer et al., 2019.

claim: CCR7 is stimulated by two endogenous chemokines CCL19 and CCL21 equally effective at 100 nM.
source: This receptor is an ideal model receptor to study endosomal G protein signaling as it is known to be active at endomembranes (Laufer et al., 2019) and is stimulated by two endogenous chemokines CCL19 and CCL21 equally effective at 100 nM (Kohout et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Kohout et al., 2004.

claim: CCL19 robustly stimulates Gi/o signaling, receptor phosphorylation, βarr recruitment, and CCR7 internalization.
source: Compared with the full agonist CCL19 that robustly stimulates Gi/o signaling, receptor phosphorylation, βarr recruitment, and CCR7 internalization, the agonist CCL21 promotes full Gi/o protein activation but only partial receptor phosphorylation, βarr recruitment, and internalization of CCR7 (Kohout et al., 2004; Zidar et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kohout et al., 2004 and Zidar et al., 2009.

claim: CCL21 promotes full Gi/o protein activation but only partial receptor phosphorylation, βarr recruitment, and internalization of CCR7.
source: Compared with the full agonist CCL19 that robustly stimulates Gi/o signaling, receptor phosphorylation, βarr recruitment, and CCR7 internalization, the agonist CCL21 promotes full Gi/o protein activation but only partial receptor phosphorylation, βarr recruitment, and internalization of CCR7 (Kohout et al., 2004; Zidar et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kohout et al., 2004 and Zidar et al., 2009.

claim: CCL19 stimulation leads to robust βarr1/2-recruitment to the plasma membrane.
source: we confirmed that activating CCR7 by CCL19 leads to robust βarr1/2-recruitment
evidence: This is supported by EbBRET data shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: CCL21 only promotes partial βarr1/2-recruitment responses.
source: we confirmed that activating CCR7 by CCL19 leads to robust βarr1/2-recruitment, whereas CCL21 only promotes partial βarr1/2-recruitment responses (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: This is supported by EbBRET data shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: CCL19 stimulation leads to strong βarr1/2 trafficking to endosomes.
source: CCL19 stimulation leads to similar strong βarr1/2 trafficking to endosomes
evidence: This is supported by EbBRET data with rGFP-Rab5 shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: CCL21 stimulation of CCR7 only causes a minor translocation of βarr1/2 to the endosomes.
source: CCL19 stimulation leads to similar strong βarr1/2 trafficking to endosomes whereas CCL21 stimulation of CCR7 only causes a minor translocation of βarr1/2 to the endosomes (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: This is supported by EbBRET data with rGFP-Rab5 shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: CCL19-stimulation leads to robust CCR7 internalization.
source: Strong and immediate reduction in this signal was observed when the cells were stimulated with CCL19 (Figure 1E–F).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT data showing loss of CCR7-SmBiT/LgBiT-CAAX signal in Figure 1E-F.

claim: CCL21-stimulated CCR7 only leads to modest internalization with most CCR7 staying at the plasma membrane.
source: In contrast, CCL21-stimulated CCR7 only led to a modest decrease in signal suggesting that CCL19-stimulation leads to robust CCR7 internalization whereas most CCR7 stays at the plasma membrane upon CCL21 activation (Figure 1E–F).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT data showing modest loss of CCR7-SmBiT/LgBiT-CAAX signal in Figure 1E-F.

claim: CCL19 stimulation leads to robust increase in CCR7 trafficking to early endosomes.
source: In this case, CCL19 stimulation led to a robust increase in luminescence
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT data showing gain of CCR7-SmBiT/LgBiT-FYVE signal in Figure 1G-H.

claim: CCL21 activation only leads to partial increase in CCR7 trafficking to early endosomes.
source: whereas CCL21 activation only led to a partial increase in the signal (Figure 1G–H).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT data showing modest gain of CCR7-SmBiT/LgBiT-FYVE signal in Figure 1G-H.

claim: CCL19 and CCL21 stimulation inhibit forskolin-induced cAMP production to a similar extent in HEK293-CCR7 cells.
source: In contrast to βarrs recruitment and receptor internalization, CCL19 and CCL21 challenge inhibited forskolin-induced cAMP production to a similar extent in HEK293-CCR7 cells (Figure 1I–J)
evidence: This is supported by CAMYEL cAMP assay data shown in Figure 1I-J.

claim: CCL19 and CCL21 act as full agonists in stimulating Gi/o signaling.
source: This supports previous observations, which suggest that both CCL19 and CCL21 act as full agonists in stimulating Gi/o signaling (Kohout et al., 2004; Zidar et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kohout et al., 2004 and Zidar et al., 2009, as well as the cAMP data in Figure 1I-J.

claim: CCR7-mediated Gi/o signaling is sustained throughout the experiment and not acutely desensitized by βarrs recruitment and/or receptor internalization.
source: Interestingly, this Gi/o signaling was sustained throughout the experiment and not acutely desensitized by βarrs recruitment and/or receptor internalization as other receptor systems (Figure 1I–J; Violin et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by the sustained cAMP inhibition shown in Figure 1I-J and comparison to Violin et al., 2008.

claim: CCL19 and CCL21 stimulate βarr1-ΔFL recruitment to CCR7 at the membrane.
source: Interestingly, both CCL19 and CCL21 stimulation led to the recruitment of βarr1-ΔFL to CCR7 at the membrane although CCL19 promoted this recruitment to a significantly higher degree than CCL21 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by EbBRET data with βarr1-ΔFL shown in Figure 2B.

claim: CCL19 promotes βarr1-ΔFL recruitment to CCR7 to a significantly higher degree than CCL21.
source: Interestingly, both CCL19 and CCL21 stimulation led to the recruitment of βarr1-ΔFL to CCR7 at the membrane although CCL19 promoted this recruitment to a significantly higher degree than CCL21 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by EbBRET data with βarr1-ΔFL shown in Figure 2B.

claim: CCL19 and CCL21 stimulation promotes βarr1-ΔFL translocation to endosomes.
source: Furthermore, CCL19 and CCL21 stimulation promotes βarr1-ΔFL translocation to endosomes (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by EbBRET data with βarr1-ΔFL and rGFP-Rab5 shown in Figure 2B.

claim: CCR7 can form tail conformation complexes with βarr1 in cells.
source: These results indicate that CCR7 can form tail conformation complexes with βarr1 in cells
evidence: This is inferred from the βarr1-ΔFL recruitment data in Figure 2B, as βarr1-ΔFL can only bind in tail conformation.

claim: The stability of the CCR7-βarr1 tail conformation complex is sufficiently strong for βarr1 to internalize the receptor into endosomes.
source: These results indicate that CCR7 can form tail conformation complexes with βarr1 in cells and that the stability of this complex is sufficiently strong for βarr1 to internalize the receptor into endosomes.
evidence: This is inferred from the βarr1-ΔFL translocation to endosomes shown in Figure 2B.

claim: CCL19-stimulation leads to a robust increase in luminescence between SmBiT-βarr1 and LgBiT-miniGi.
source: In HEK293-CCR7 cells expressing SmBiT-βarr1 and LgBiT-miniGi, CCL19-stimulation leads to a robust increase in luminescence (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-C.

claim: CCL19-stimulated CCR7 recruits Gi/o and βarrs simultaneously.
source: These results indicate that CCL19-stimulated CCR7 recruits Gi/o and βarrs simultaneously.
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT data showing proximity between SmBiT-βarr1 and LgBiT-miniGi in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B-C.

claim: Both CCL19 and CCL21 stimulated co-coupling of Gi/o and βarrs to CCR7.
source: Interestingly, both CCL19 and CCL21 stimulated co-coupling of Gi/o and βarrs to CCR7, although CCL19 promoted the formation of these complexes to a significantly larger degree than CCL21 (Figure 2D–E).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT data comparing CCL19 and CCL21 responses shown in Figure 2D-E.

claim: CCL19 promotes the formation of CCR7-Gi/o-βarr complexes to a significantly larger degree than CCL21.
source: Interestingly, both CCL19 and CCL21 stimulated co-coupling of Gi/o and βarrs to CCR7, although CCL19 promoted the formation of these complexes to a significantly larger degree than CCL21 (Figure 2D–E).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT data comparing CCL19 and CCL21 responses shown in Figure 2D-E.

claim: CCL19-CCR7 recruits βarr2-Strawberry and Halo-miniGi to endosomal-shaped intracellular locations.
source: In this setup, CCL19-CCR7 recruited βarr2-Strawberry and Halo-miniGi to endosomal-shaped intracellular locations whereas this co-localization was minor for CCL21-CCR7 (Figure 2F–G).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2F-G.

claim: CCL21-CCR7 shows minor co-localization of βarr2-Strawberry and Halo-miniGi at endosomes.
source: In this setup, CCL19-CCR7 recruited βarr2-Strawberry and Halo-miniGi to endosomal-shaped intracellular locations whereas this co-localization was minor for CCL21-CCR7 (Figure 2F–G).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2F-G.

claim: CCL19 stimulation leads to robust endosomal and CCR7-mediated recruitment of Gi/o and βarr1.
source: Together, these results indicate that CCL19 stimulation leads to robust endosomal and CCR7-mediated recruitment of Gi/o and βarr1.
evidence: This is supported by the confocal microscopy data in Figure 2F-G showing co-localization at endosomes.

claim: Both CCL19 and CCL21 stimulate the recruitment of Rap1GAP-SmBiT to LgBiT-FYVE in HEK293-CCR7 cells.
source: Using this approach, we observed that both CCL19 and CCL21 stimulate the recruitment of Rap1GAP-SmBiT to LgBiT-FYVE in HEK293-CCR7 cells (Figure 3B–C).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT data showing endosomal Gi/o activation in Figure 3B-C.

claim: CCL19 facilitates endosomal Gi/o activation to a significantly higher degree as compared to CCL21.
source: Similar to CCR7 internalization, CCL19 facilitated this response to a significantly higher degree as compared to CCL21 (Figure 3B–C).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT data comparing CCL19 and CCL21 responses in Figure 3B-C.

claim: The recruitment of Rap1GAP-SmBiT to LgBiT-FYVE is blunted by the Gi/o inhibitor pertussis toxin (PTX).
source: In addition, the recruitment of Rap1GAP-SmBiT to LgBiT-FYVE was blunted by the Gi/o inhibitor pertussis toxin (PTX), and was not observed in mock-transfected HEK293 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT data with PTX treatment shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: Internalized CCR7 promotes endosomal Gi/o activation.
source: These results indicate that internalized CCR7 promotes endosomal Gi/o activation.
evidence: This is inferred from the Rap1GAP-SmBiT/LgBiT-FYVE data in Figure 3B-C showing Gi/o activation at endosomes.

claim: CCL19 stimulation leads to a strong and significant increase in EbBRET signaling between RlucII-miniGi and rGFP-Rab5a.
source: Using this approach, CCL19 stimulation led to a strong and significant increase in EbBRET signaling between RlucII-miniGi and rGFP-Rab5a indicating that CCL19-bound CCR7 indeed activates Gi/o robustly from endosomes (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by EbBRET data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: CCL19-bound CCR7 activates Gi/o robustly from endosomes.
source: Using this approach, CCL19 stimulation led to a strong and significant increase in EbBRET signaling between RlucII-miniGi and rGFP-Rab5a indicating that CCL19-bound CCR7 indeed activates Gi/o robustly from endosomes (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by EbBRET data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: CCL21 stimulation provokes a small yet significant increase in EbBRET response between RlucII-miniGi and rGFP-Rab5a.
source: In contrast, CCL21 stimulation provoked a small yet significant increase in EbBRET response, demonstrating that Gi/o protein is activated from endosomes by CCL21-bound CCR7 to a minor extent (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by EbBRET data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Gi/o protein is activated from endosomes by CCL21-bound CCR7 to a minor extent.
source: In contrast, CCL21 stimulation provoked a small yet significant increase in EbBRET response, demonstrating that Gi/o protein is activated from endosomes by CCL21-bound CCR7 to a minor extent (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by EbBRET data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: CCR7 activation with either CCL19 or CCL21 leads to the recruitment of Halo-miniGi to the cell surface.
source: In cells expressing RFP-Lck, CCR7 activation with either CCL19 or CCL21 leads to the recruitment of Halo-miniGi to the cell surface (Figure 3F–G).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3F-G.

claim: No significant difference between CCL19- and CCL21-stimulated translocation of Halo-miniGi to the plasma membrane was detected.
source: As expected, no significant difference between CCL19- and CCL21-stimulated translocation of Halo-miniGi to the plasma membrane was detected.
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3F-G.

claim: Activation by CCL19, and to a minor degree CCL21, results in co-localization of Halo-miniGi and RFP-EEA1 at endosomes.
source: However, in cells expressing RFP-EEA1, activation by CCL19, and to a minor degree CCL21, resulted in co-localization of Halo-miniGi and RFP-EEA1 at endosomes (Figure 3H–I).
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3H-I.

claim: CCL19-CCR7 promotes robust G protein activation from endosomes.
source: Together these results suggest that CCL19-CCR7 promotes robust G protein activation from endosomes
evidence: This is supported by multiple lines of evidence including EbBRET, NanoBiT, and confocal microscopy data in Figure 3.

claim: CCL21-CCR7 predominantly activates Gi/o at the cell surface and to a modest degree from endosomes.
source: whereas CCL21-CCR7 predominantly activates Gi/o at the cell surface and to a modest degree from endosomes.
evidence: This is supported by multiple lines of evidence including EbBRET, NanoBiT, and confocal microscopy data in Figure 3.

claim: A total of 584 proteins were identified whose enrichment was changed significantly upon stimulation with either CCL19 or CCL21 (p<0.05 and change in intensity of log2>1).
source: From the MS profiling, we identified a total of 584 proteins, whose enrichment was changed significantly upon stimulation with either CCL19 or CCL21 (p<0.05 and change in intensity of log2>1) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: Among robustly enriched proteins by CCR7 activation, several are involved in functions related to vesicle trafficking, signal transduction, cytoskeletal dynamics, and cell migration.
source: Among robustly enriched proteins by CCR7 activation, several are involved in functions related to vesicle trafficking, signal transduction, cytoskeletal dynamics, and cell migration among others (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by APEX2 proteomics data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Proteins enriched by both ENDO-APEX2 and chemokine-stimulated CCR7-APEX2 include SNX3, RAB9A, ARH, and CCD93.
source: Proteins enriched by both ENDO-APEX2 (as compared to both CYTO-APEX2 and PM-APEX2) and chemokine-stimulated CCR7-APEX2 include SNX3, RAB9A, ARH, and CCD93 (Figure 5A and D).
evidence: This is supported by APEX2 proteomics data comparing spatial references shown in Figure 5A and D.

claim: Proteins involved in receptor and vesicular trafficking including RIC1, SNX17, VA0D1, ARRB2, and DYN3 were enriched over the entire time course of CCR7 activation.
source: As expected, proteins involved in receptor and vesicular trafficking including RIC1, SNX17, VA0D1, ARRB2, and DYN3, among others, were enriched over the entire time course of CCR7 activation (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by APEX2 proteomics data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Most receptor and vesicular trafficking proteins were more enriched by CCL19 stimulation as compared to the CCL21 challenge.
source: Most of these proteins were more enriched by CCL19 stimulation as compared to the CCL21 challenge.
evidence: This is supported by APEX2 proteomics data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Endosomal proteins such as STX7, STX12, SNX3, and VTI1B were enriched for both CCL19 and CCL21 stimulation.
source: In addition, we observed enrichment of endosomal proteins such as STX7, STX12, SNX3, and VTI1B for both CCL19 and CCL21 stimulation (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by APEX2 proteomics data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Proteins involved in lysosomal trafficking including LAMP1, VPS16, VAMP7, WDR91, and PP4P1 were enriched by CCL19 and to a lesser degree by CCL21 after 25 min of stimulation.
source: Interestingly, proteins involved in lysosomal trafficking including LAMP1, VPS16, VAMP7, WDR91, and PP4P1 were enriched by CCL19 and to a lesser degree by CCL21 after 25 min of stimulation (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by APEX2 proteomics data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Proteins involved in receptor trafficking via recycling endosomes or the trans-Golgi network such as SNX6, RAB7L, and GGA3 were enriched at the later stages of CCR7 activation particularly when stimulated with CCL21.
source: Proteins involved in receptor trafficking via recycling endosomes or the trans-Golgi network such as SNX6, RAB7L, and GGA3 were also enriched at the later stages of CCR7 activation particularly when stimulated with CCL21 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by APEX2 proteomics data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Proteins associated with the Golgi network (SNX3, COG5, YIF1A, SC22B, and AP3S1) were enriched by either CCL19 or CCL21 suggesting general CCR7 trafficking to this subcellular compartment.
source: In addition to these, proteins associated with the Golgi network (SNX3, COG5, YIF1A, SC22B, and AP3S1) were enriched by either CCL19 or CCL21 suggesting general CCR7 trafficking to this subcellular compartment as previously reported (Laufer et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by APEX2 proteomics data shown in Figure 5A and citation to Laufer et al., 2019.

claim: The trafficking pattern of CCR7 upon chemokine stimulation is tightly regulated between lysosomal degradation and recycling.
source: These results indicate that the trafficking pattern of CCR7 upon chemokine stimulation is tightly regulated between lysosomal degradation and recycling.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential enrichment of lysosomal and recycling proteins shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Robust enrichment of proteins regulating inositol 1,4,5-triphosphate signaling (ERLN1/2, IP3KA), diacylglycerol signaling (DGKQ), calcium mobilization at the endoplasmic reticulum (TMCO1), and activity of the Rho GTPases was observed.
source: Among enriched signaling proteins, we observed robust enrichment of proteins regulating inositol 1,4,5-triphosphate signaling (ERLN1/2, IP3KA), diacylglycerol signaling (DGKQ), calcium mobilization at the endoplasmic reticulum (TMCO1), and activity of the Rho GTPases (Figure 5A and E–G).
evidence: This is supported by APEX2 proteomics data shown in Figure 5A and E-G.

claim: EYA2 was enriched by CCR7 activation.
source: Another interesting signaling protein enriched by CCR7 activation includes a member of the eyes absent (EYA) subfamily of protein, EYA2.
evidence: This is supported by APEX2 proteomics data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: EYA2 has been shown to interact with and regulate Gαi/o and Gαz subunits.
source: This protein has been shown to interact with and regulate Gαi/o and Gαz subunits (Embry et al., 2004; Fan et al., 2000)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Embry et al., 2004 and Fan et al., 2000.

claim: EYA4 was recently identified in a similar APEX2-based study of the μ-opioid receptor.
source: and EYA4, a member of the same family, was recently identified in a similar APEX2-based study of the μ-opioid receptor (Polacco et al., 2024).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Polacco et al., 2024.

claim: GRIP2, MARK4, and EI24 were detected as being among the highest levels of enrichment regardless of the activation ligand or time.
source: We also detected three novel interaction partners GRIP2, MARK4, and EI24 as being among the highest levels regardless of the activation ligand or time (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by APEX2 proteomics data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: A number of Rho GTPase regulators are enriched by chemokine-stimulation of CCR7.
source: Our APEX2-based proteomics results demonstrate that a number of these Rho GTPase regulators are enriched by chemokine-stimulation of CCR7, and thus, potentially form part of larger CCR7 signalosomes that control downstream Rho GTPase activity (Figure 5F–G).
evidence: This is supported by APEX2 proteomics data shown in Figure 5F-G.

claim: Some Rho GTPase regulators, including RHG26, ARG28, RHG29, ACK1, and BORG5, were differentially enriched upon CCL19 or CCL21 stimulation.
source: Interestingly, some of these regulators, including RHG26, ARG28, RHG29, ACK1, and BORG5, were differentially enriched upon CCL19 or CCL21 stimulation (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is supported by APEX2 proteomics data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Both CCL19 and CCL21 stimulated RhoA and Cdc42 activation to a similar extent.
source: Using this setup, we found that both CCL19 and CCL21 stimulated RhoA and Cdc42 activation to a similar extent, which indicates that the spatial aspect of G protein activation does not appear to influence RhoA and Cdc42 signaling (Figure 6B–C , and F–G).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT assay data shown in Figure 6B-C and F-G.

claim: The spatial aspect of G protein activation does not appear to influence RhoA and Cdc42 signaling.
source: Using this setup, we found that both CCL19 and CCL21 stimulated RhoA and Cdc42 activation to a similar extent, which indicates that the spatial aspect of G protein activation does not appear to influence RhoA and Cdc42 signaling (Figure 6B–C , and F–G).
evidence: This is inferred from the similar RhoA and Cdc42 activation by CCL19 and CCL21 shown in Figure 6B-C and F-G.

claim: CCL19 promoted Rac1 signaling to a significantly greater extent than CCL21 stimulation.
source: In contrast, CCL19 promoted Rac1 signaling to a significantly greater extent than CCL21 stimulation (Figure 6D–E).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT assay data shown in Figure 6D-E.

claim: CCR7-stimulated Rac1 signaling is mediated via a Gi/o-dependent mechanism.
source: Pre-incubating the HEK293-CCR7 cells with the Gi/o inhibitor PTX, virtually eliminated the chemokine-induced activation of Rac1, indicating that CCR7-stimulateted Rac1 signaling is mediated via a Gi/o-dependent mechanism (Figure 6H–I).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT assay data with PTX treatment shown in Figure 6H-I.

claim: Pre-treatment of HEK293-CCR7 cells with the endocytosis inhibitor Dyngo-4a reduced chemokine-stimulated CCR7 internalization and Rac1 activation robustly.
source: Interestingly, pre-treatment of the HEK293-CCR7 cells with the endocytosis inhibitor Dyngo-4a (Jensen et al., 2017) reduced chemokine-stimulated CCR7 internalization and Rac1 activation robustly (Figure 6J-K, Figure 6—figure supplement 1G-H).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT assay data with Dyngo-4a treatment shown in Figure 6J-K and Figure 6—figure supplement 1G-H.

claim: Overexpression of the hemagglutinin-tagged dominant negative dynamin 1 K44A mutant (HA-Dyn-K44A) diminished chemokine-activated CCR7 internalization and Rac1 activity.
source: Furthermore, overexpression of the hemagglutinin-tagged dominant negative dynamin 1 K44A mutant (HA-Dyn-K44A) diminished chemokine-activated CCR7 internalization and Rac1 activity suggesting that CCR7-mediated Rac1 activation depends on receptor internalization (Figure 6L-M, Figure 6—figure supplement 1I-K).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT assay data with HA-Dyn-K44A overexpression shown in Figure 6L-M and Figure 6—figure supplement 1I-K.

claim: CCR7-mediated Rac1 activation depends on receptor internalization.
source: Furthermore, overexpression of the hemagglutinin-tagged dominant negative dynamin 1 K44A mutant (HA-Dyn-K44A) diminished chemokine-activated CCR7 internalization and Rac1 activity suggesting that CCR7-mediated Rac1 activation depends on receptor internalization (Figure 6L-M, Figure 6—figure supplement 1I-K).
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing that blocking internalization reduces Rac1 activation in Figure 6L-M and Figure 6—figure supplement 1I-K.

claim: Pre-incubating cells with the endocytosis inhibitor PitStop2 led to a severe reduction in chemokine-stimulated CCR7 internalization and Rac1 activity.
source: Also, pre-incubating the cells with the endocytosis inhibitor PitStop2, which acts on clathrin rather than dynamin, led to a severe reduction in chemokine-stimulated CCR7 internalization and Rac1 activity (Figure 6N-O, Figure 6—figure supplement 1L-M).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT assay data with PitStop2 treatment shown in Figure 6N-O and Figure 6—figure supplement 1L-M.

claim: The CCR7-ΔST construct expresses well at the cell surface but does not internalize upon CCL19 stimulation.
source: Finally, we mutated all potential serine/threonine phosphorylation sites in the carboxy-terminal tail of CCR7 and found that this CCR7-ΔST construct expresses well at the cell surface, but does not internalize upon CCL19 stimulation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1N-P).
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT assay data with CCR7-ΔST shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1N-P.

claim: The ability of CCR7-ΔST to activate Rac1 in response to chemokine-stimulation is severely reduced as compared to wild-type CCR7.
source: When expressed in HEK293 cells, the ability of CCR7-ΔST to activate Rac1 in response to chemokine-stimulation is severely reduced as compared to wild-type CCR7.
evidence: This is supported by NanoBiT assay data comparing CCR7 and CCR7-ΔST shown in Figure 6P-Q.

claim: Signaling by internalized CCR7 is a mechanism to activate Rac1.
source: These results suggest that signaling by internalized CCR7 is a mechanism to activate Rac1.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing that blocking internalization or removing phosphorylation sites reduces Rac1 activation in Figure 6.

claim: CCL19 and CCL21 stimulation leads to similar inhibition of forskolin-stimulated cAMP production in Jurkat T cells.
source: As in HEK293-CCR7 cells, CCL19, and CCL21 stimulation led to similar inhibition of forskolin-stimulated cAMP production in Jurkat T cells confirming that CCR7 activation by either chemokine results in comparable stimulation of Gi/o signaling (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by cAMP assay data in Jurkat T cells shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Jurkat T cells migrated more efficiently towards a gradient of CCL19 as compared with CCL21.
source: Interestingly, Jurkat T cells migrated more efficiently towards a gradient of CCL19 as compared with CCL21, which was assessed by the transwell chemotaxis assay (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by transwell migration assay data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Pre-treatment with the Gi/o inhibitor PTX almost completely abolished the ability of Jurkat T cells to migrate towards both CCL19 and CCL21.
source: To test this hypothesis, we pre-treated the Jurkat T cells with the Gi/o inhibitor PTX, which almost completely abolished the ability of the cells to migrate towards both CCL19 and CCL21 (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is supported by transwell migration assay data with PTX treatment shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Pre-incubation with the endocytosis inhibitors Dyngo-4a or PitStop2 led to a significant reduction in chemotaxis of both CCL19 and CCL21-stimulated cells.
source: Interestingly, pre-incubation with the endocytosis inhibitors Dyngo-4a or PitStop2 led to a significant reduction in chemotaxis of both CCL19 and CCL21-stimulated cells as compared to the inactive Dyngo or PitNot compounds, respectively (Figure 7D–E).
evidence: This is supported by transwell migration assay data with endocytosis inhibitors shown in Figure 7D-E.

claim: Pre-treatment with the Rac1 inhibitor EHT1864 reduced Jurkat T-cell chemotaxis towards both CCL19 and CCL21.
source: Finally, as CCR7-mediated endosomal Gi/o signaling was shown to enhance Rac1 activity, we pre-treated Jurkat T-cells with the Rac1 inhibitor EHT1864. As expected, EHT1864 reduced Jurkat T-cell chemotaxis towards both CCL19 and CCL21 (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is supported by transwell migration assay data with EHT1864 treatment shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Endosomal Gi/o signaling by internalized CCR7 promotes chemotaxis of Jurkat T cells.
source: Collectively, these findings suggest that endosomal Gi/o signaling by internalized CCR7 promotes chemotaxis of Jurkat T cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing that blocking endocytosis or Gi/o signaling reduces chemotaxis in Figure 7.

claim: Removing the carboxy-terminal tail or mutating its phosphorylation sites in the chemokine receptors CXCR1-4 reduces their ability to internalize and promote cellular chemotaxis towards a chemokine-gradient.
source: In fact, removing the carboxy-terminal tail or mutating its phosphorylation sites in the chemokine receptors CXCR1-4 reduces their ability to internalize and promote cellular chemotaxis towards a chemokine-gradient (Roland et al., 2003; Richardson et al., 2003; Colvin et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Roland et al., 2003; Richardson et al., 2003; Colvin et al., 2004.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of endocytosis reduces Akt signaling and chemotaxis of immune cells towards gradients of different chemokines.
source: Similar reduction in Akt signaling and chemotaxis of immune cells towards gradients of different chemokines were observed upon pharmacological inhibition of endocytosis (Jacques et al., 2015; English et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jacques et al., 2015 and English et al., 2018.

claim: Removal of intracellular loops in CXCR4 reduces G protein activation and is associated with decreased capacity of CXCR4 to promote cell migration.
source: Additionally, removal of intracellular loops in CXCR4 reduces G protein activation and is associated with decreased capacity of CXCR4 to promote cell migration indicating a co-dependency of G protein signaling and receptor internalization on this cell physiological function (Roland et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Roland et al., 2003.

claim: The chemokine receptor CCR1 displays constitutive G protein activation and internalization in HEK293 cells by a mechanism where Gαi/o and βarr complex with the receptor simultaneously.
source: Notably, the chemokine receptor CCR1 displays constitutive G protein activation and internalization in HEK293 cells by a mechanism where Gαi/o and βarr complex with the receptor simultaneously (Gilliland et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gilliland et al., 2013.

claim: Constitutive CCR1-mediated G protein activation from internalized compartment was reported to stimulate cell migration.
source: This constitutive CCR1-mediated G protein activation from internalized compartment was reported to stimulate cell migration.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gilliland et al., 2013.

claim: Sustained Gi/o signaling by internalized sphingosine-1-phophate type 1 receptor has been shown to promote cell migration in human umbilical vein endothelial cells.
source: Finally, sustained Gi/o signaling by internalized sphingosine-1-phophate type 1 receptor has been shown to promote cell migration in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (Mullershausen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Mullershausen et al., 2009.

claim: GRIP2 has been shown to bind AMPA ionotropic glutamate receptors via PDZ-domains to regulate their intracellular trafficking.
source: GRIP2 has been shown to bind AMPA ionotropic glutamate receptors via PDZ-domains to regulate their intracellular trafficking (Mao et al., 2010; Dong et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Mao et al., 2010 and Dong et al., 1999.

claim: EI24 is a protein whose expression is enhanced by p53 activation, and plays a role in growth suppression and apoptosis as well as in autophagy through formation of degradative autolysosomes.
source: EI24 is a protein whose expression is enhanced by p53 activation, and plays a role in growth suppression and apoptosis as well as in autophagy through formation of degradative autolysosomes (Tian et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tian et al., 2010.

claim: EYA2 can interact directly with Gαi/o and Gαz subunits and regulate their activity.
source: Interestingly, EYA2 can interact directly with Gαi/o and Gαz subunits and regulate their activity (Embry et al., 2004; Fan et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Embry et al., 2004 and Fan et al., 2000.

claim: EYA2 interaction with Gαi/o and Gαz prevents their translocation to the nucleus, and thus, blocks their role as transcription co-factors.
source: This interaction prevents their translocation to the nucleus, and thus, block their role as transcription co-factors (Embry et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Embry et al., 2004.

claim: Rac1 can be activated in endosomes by RhoGEFs such as Tiam1 and Vav1.
source: Rac1 plays a key role in cell migration, which we further demonstrated in this study (Figure 7F), and can be activated in endosomes by RhoGEFs such as Tiam1 and Vav1 (Palamidessi et al., 2008; Laufer et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Palamidessi et al., 2008 and Laufer et al., 2019.

claim: A chemokine-stimulated association between CCR7 and Vav1 at endomembranes was reported, which depends on recruitment of βarrs and Src.
source: Previously, a chemokine-stimulated association between CCR7 and Vav1 at endomembranes was reported, which depends on recruitment of βarrs and Src (Laufer et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Laufer et al., 2019.

claim: The CCR7-Vav1 signaling complex was shown to directly activate Rac1.
source: The formation of this signaling complex was shown to directly activate Rac1.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Laufer et al., 2019.

claim: The formation of the CCR7-Vav1 signaling complex did not depend on Gi/o protein and occurred mostly at the Golgi network.
source: In contrast to our findings, the formation of this signaling complex did not depend on Gi/o protein and occurred mostly at the Golgi network (Laufer et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Laufer et al., 2019.

claim: Activation of Rac1 leads to its translocation to the cell surface via recycling endosomes.
source: Activation of Rac1 leads to its translocation to the cell surface via recycling endosomes, a process reported to occur in response to stimulation of CCR7 as well as several receptor tyrosine kinases (Figure 7G; Palamidessi et al., 2008; Laufer et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Palamidessi et al., 2008 and Laufer et al., 2019.

claim: From the cell surface, Rac1 activates the major effector PAK1, which phosphorylates LIM kinase and cortactin to coordinate actin polymerization at the plasma membrane region.
source: From this subcellular region, Rac1 activates the major effector PAK1, which phosphorylates LIM kinase and cortactin, among others, to coordinate actin polymerization at the plasma membrane region (Tebar et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tebar et al., 2018.

claim: Actin polymerization leads to formation of cytoskeletal actin filaments that serve as underlying stabilizing structures of newly formed filopodia and lamellipodia.
source: This polymerization leads to formation of cytoskeletal actin filaments that serve as underlying stabilizing structures of newly formed filopodia and lamellipodia (Tebar et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Tebar et al., 2018.

claim: Membrane protrusions constitute a major mechanistic step during cell migration.
source: As these membrane protrusions constitute a major mechanistic step during cell migration, endosomal Rac1 activation plays a central role in this cell physiological process (Schiefermeier et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schiefermeier et al., 2011.

claim: Endosomal Rac1 activation plays a central role in cell migration.
source: As these membrane protrusions constitute a major mechanistic step during cell migration, endosomal Rac1 activation plays a central role in this cell physiological process (Schiefermeier et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schiefermeier et al., 2011.

claim: CCL19's superior ability to promote chemotaxis of CCR7-expressing cells as compared to CCL21 has previously been reported.
source: Similar findings that demonstrate CCL19's superior ability to promote chemotaxis of other CCR7-expressing cells as compared to CCL21 have previously been reported (Kohout et al., 2004; Hjortø et al., 2016; Ricart et al., 2011; Jørgensen et al., 2018; Bardi et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kohout et al., 2004; Hjortø et al., 2016; Ricart et al., 2011; Jørgensen et al., 2018; Bardi et al., 2001.
